sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r7/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 2 (#1 instruction_is_a_natural_product_request) and Internal Quality Checks row 2 (same wording, no extra annotation)
evidence: Read cold, instruction.md (5 prose paragraphs, lines 1-9) is a first-person firm request: line 1 'Kittle & Rowe is a small law firm, and our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last. We want a secure chat where each client talks to us inside their legal matter...'; line 3 states priorities as business concerns ('Two things matter more than anything else. First, ethical walls... Second, retention...'); line 9 'Before you hand it over, please try it the way we'll use it, in a browser'. A grep for numbered items, bullets, 'shall' and spec tables finds none; the only 'must' (line 3) is a conversational statement of a conduct concern, not a spec clause. No framework, file layout or endpoint list appears in instruction.md; the only paths are the template-mandated deliverable/seed/notes locations (/assets/seed_data.json, /instructions, /app/server.js, /app/app.db, line 5). Runtime facts (Node 22, port 3000, Express/better-sqlite3 preinstalled, /api/health, DB_PATH, fixed clock) are confined to the notes file integration.md, phrased as 'How we run it', which is the runtime contract row 4 requires rather than a build recipe; walls-and-retention.md and conversations.md are dense but written as house rules in the firm's voice ('Our clients ask several things at once, so answers have to stay with their question'), with one account table that is credentials data, not a feature matrix. Weak/alternative probe: this row grades prose form, not app behavior, so no broken app can pass or conforming app fail through it; the only plausible defect reading (notes as a disguised acceptance checklist) is a density/voice concern for rows 2 and 6, not a spec-sheet or recipe form. Not exercised by runtime (none needed for this row).
